A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and appendices. The original material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, including Appendices A–C; v2 adds Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM hidden-state measurements, teacher–student training experiments, and analyses fitting scaling laws to reconstructed Chinchilla data.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds fitting-validation results, bootstrap estimates, and a causal-tracing experiment on Pythia models.

M1.justification: The additive scaling model, teacher–student residual architecture, KL/MSE training objectives, and higher-order block variant remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendix C. Causal tracing is an added diagnostic experiment rather than a modification of the proposed model.

E1.justification: v2 adds a factual-recall scenario using the Space Needle/Seattle prompt with corrupted embeddings and restored hidden states (Appendix D). This is a limited extension of test conditions; the FineWeb, reconstructed Chinchilla, and synthetic teacher–student coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The existing comparison conditions are retained, with no new competing method evaluated against the proposed model. Meng et al.'s causal tracing is adopted as a diagnostic, while their memory-editing results are discussed rather than independently benchmarked.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with random 80/20 held-out validation of the 203 fitting points and clean, corrupted, and individually patched forward passes across six Pythia models. The latter measures Seattle prediction probability under controlled embedding noise. Existing primary training settings and the exclusion of 40 high-loss points remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds exclusion-threshold sensitivity, displays the excluded observations, and reports held-out and bootstrap robustness checks. Figure 6 and Appendix D add a causal-tracing case study testing functional layer groups. Together these substantially expand analyses of fitting reliability and the proposed mechanism.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained Jacobian-based standard errors and teacher replicates, v2 reports variation across ten random validation splits and 200 bootstrap resamples. Means and standard deviations now quantify predictive-error variability and empirical stability of the fitted exponents.

E6.justification: v2 adds training/test relative errors of 0.41% ± 0.02% and 0.40% ± 0.07%, plus bootstrap means/SDs of 1.00 ± 0.04, 1.01 ± 0.02, and 0.30 ± 0.02 for width, depth, and data exponents. It also adds exclusion-sensitivity findings and two-group tracing results, informative only for Pythia-12B. These are new supporting results; the original headline estimates and toy-model results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 6 adds the deduction that inverse width/depth scaling, m proportional to depth, and N proportional to m squared times depth imply N^(-1/3) model-size scaling. The original error-accumulation and discretization arguments, including the higher-order analysis in Appendix C, remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and three boxed results retain the inverse-depth and ensemble-averaging claims. Section 6 adds a concluding claim that inverse-depth scaling can explain the approximately one-third parameter-count exponent observed in Chinchilla scaling.

C2.justification: v1 already allowed multiple functional ensembles. v2 develops this into an explicit weaker form of compositionality, interprets tracing patterns as noisy redundancy within groups, and states that geometric measurements cannot identify individual layer functions. Appendix D also explains why smaller models provide uninformative traces.

D1.justification: v2 adds script references for sensitivity, validation, bootstrap, and tracing analyses, plus the tracing prompt, model list, Gaussian-noise scale, fixed-noise control, and batching procedure. Appendix B.1 corrects the displayed fitting objective to log both observed and predicted loss, matching the earlier prose; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds Meng et al. (2022a, 2022b) and connects the functional-group interpretation to factual-memory localization and multilayer editing. The broader research positioning remains intact. The publication update for Liu et al. (2025a) concerns an already cited work.

P1.justification: Changes are concentrated in the expanded discussion, added Appendix D, additional Appendix B.3 paragraphs, and a generic Impact Statement. The contribution box is repositioned and front matter updated, while most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the causal-tracing heatmap in Figure 6, exclusion-sensitivity plots in Figure 17, and excluded-point overlays in Figure 18. Existing figures are retained and renumbered, with appendix figures redistributed across pages; the overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity, held-out validation, and bootstrap checks make the central scaling fit more assessable than in v1, while the corrected objective improves clarity. The documented tracing example also adds useful evidence, but it uses one prompt and is informative only for Pythia-12B, leaving broad mechanistic conclusions provisional. These are useful, bounded gains in reliability and transparency.
